Obtain focused history and physical exam to assess for contraindications to stress testing.
Are there symptoms and/or clinical findings warranting coronary angiography?
Refer to cardiology for angiography.

Is the patient a candidate for a revascularization procedure?

cell.label: Patient with known ischemic heart disease
Obtain focused history, physical exam, and review of medication and reversible risk factors.
Are there acute symptoms, changes in symptoms, or inadequately controlled symptoms?
Assess for acute coronary syndrome or unstable angina.
Are there indications for assessment of LV function (eg, signs or symptoms of CHF)?
Assess LV function.
Is LVEF <0.40 (moderate or severe LV dysfunction)?
Ensure pharmacotherapy for CHF/LV dysfunction.
Consider cardiac stress test.
Indication for noninvasive cardiac stress test?
IHD patient with optimally controlled ischemic symptoms or no symptoms, with or without prior event.
Do test results indicate diagnosis of CAD with high/intense features, or intermediate?
Refer to cardiology for possible angiography.
Is patient at high risk for sudden cardiac death? Or other indication for referral to cardiology?
Refer to cardiology for evaluation and/or revascularization.
Continue aspirin and beta-adrenergic blocking agent.
Does patient have LDL-C >100 mg/dL, HDL <40 mg/dL or elevated TG?
Initiate therapy to address lipid abnormalities.
Is patient hypertensive ( ie, blood pressure >140/90)?
Control hypertension.
Is patient currently using tobacco?
Initiate tobacco use cessation.
Does patient have diabetes mellitus?
Manage diabetes.
Does patient screen positive for depression?
Manage depression.
Provide patient and family education.
Consider exercise rehabilitation program.
Schedule regular follow-up.
